passage:
Dear Diary,
Today was speech day at school. Last night I told Mummy my tummy hurt. It did hurt, sort of. This morning she let me stay home.
The weird thing is, the minute she said 'okay, stay home', my tummy stopped hurting. Like magic. I watched cartoons, made a jam sandwich and felt totally fine.
Afreen Didi came home and said Mrs Fernandes asked where I was. My tummy went funny again for one second.
Now I'm in bed and there's a spelling test on Monday. It's three whole days away and I'm already scared. Maybe my tummy will hurt on Monday too.
From Zubin

qa.q: What happened to Zubin's tummy when Mummy said 'okay, stay home'?
qa.a: Zubin's tummy stopped hurting, like magic.

qa.q: What does Zubin feel about Monday's spelling test, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Zubin is already scared three days early and half hopes the tummy will hurt again, which shows staying home now feels like the safe way out.

qa.q: What turning point could Mummy offer at this stage?
qa.a: She could gently notice that the ache vanished once school was off, then help Zubin go on Monday with a small plan and her support rather than another day at home.

qa.q: How might Afreen Didi see Zubin's day at home?
qa.a: Afreen Didi might be puzzled that Zubin seemed fine all day, and may wonder why the teacher had to ask.

grounding: It shows a child staying home with a tummy ache, feeling instant relief, and then finding the fear starting earlier before the next test.

passage:
On Monday morning Jatin clutched his stomach by the cowshed. 'Kaka, it hurts. I can't go.' Monday was reading-aloud day in Class 4, and last time the words had jumbled in his mouth while everyone laughed.
Ramesh Kaka felt his forehead, frowned and said, 'Then come with me to the field.'
By the time they reached the cotton rows, the pain was gone. Jatin chased a mongoose, ate a guava and felt light as a kite.
But the next Sunday, while the pressure cooker whistled for dinner, his stomach began to twist again. Tomorrow was Monday. He hadn't even thought about school yet, and already his body was saying no.

qa.q: What did Jatin do in the field once the pain was gone?
qa.a: He chased a mongoose and ate a guava.

qa.q: Why did Jatin's stomach start twisting on Sunday evening?
qa.a: Staying home had brought such quick relief that his body now linked Monday with danger, so the fear started a day early, before he even thought about school.

qa.q: What might help at this stage before the pattern grows?
qa.a: Ramesh Kaka could talk with Jatin about the reading-aloud worry and ask the teacher about a gentler way to practise, so Jatin goes to school instead of avoiding it.

qa.q: What might Ramesh Kaka be thinking as Jatin runs about the field?
qa.a: Kaka may start to wonder whether the stomach ache was really about school, since Jatin seemed perfectly well among the cotton rows.

grounding: It shows a child avoiding school through a stomach ache, feeling instant relief, and then the fear arriving earlier the next week.

passage:
Every Thursday was swimming class at the club pool, and every Thursday morning Ramesh's stomach began to hurt at breakfast.
"Amma, my tummy," he said this Thursday, holding his side.
Irawati felt his forehead. No fever. But his face was pale, so she said, "Fine, stay home today."
The moment she said it, the ache melted. Ramesh felt light, as if a heavy school bag had been lifted off his back. He spent the morning building a block tower and humming.
The next week, the ache came on Wednesday night, right after dinner. By bedtime he was curled up, sure he couldn't go.
Irawati sat on the edge of his bed, frowning. The ache was real; she could see it. But it seemed to know exactly what day it was.

qa.q: What day was swimming class?
qa.a: Every Thursday.

qa.q: How did Ramesh feel when his mother said he could stay home?
qa.a: He felt a huge relief, as if a heavy bag had been lifted, and the ache melted away.

qa.q: What could Irawati try before next Thursday?
qa.a: Stay calm and kind about the ache, talk to the swimming teacher, and help him go for part of the class so avoidance doesn't grow; if the ache keeps going or worries her, check with the doctor.

qa.q: What is Irawati noticing as she sits on his bed?
qa.a: She notices the ache is real but always arrives before swimming, and feels puzzled and worried.

grounding: A child's stomach ache lets him skip swimming, the fear drops at once, and the next week the ache starts even earlier.

passage:
"Sonali didi, I can't go to school today. My tummy hurts."
"Again? It's the third Monday."
"It really hurts! Here."
"Is it because of the dance practice for Annual Day?"
"No." Devika pulled up the blanket. "Maybe."
"I talked to Mumma. She says you can stay home today."
Devika's face changed at once. "Really?" She sat up. "Can I watch cartoons?"
"I thought your tummy hurt."
"It's... better now. A bit."
"Just like that?"
"It went away when you said I can stay."
Sonali sat down on the bed. "Devu, what do you think will happen next Monday?"
"My tummy will hurt on Sunday night," Devika said in a small voice. "Even earlier."

qa.q: What practice is Devika avoiding?
qa.a: The dance practice for Annual Day.

qa.q: Why did Devika's tummy feel better so quickly?
qa.a: She felt a rush of relief when told she could stay home, which made the fear and the ache drop at once.

qa.q: What could Sonali and Mumma do before next Monday?
qa.a: Talk gently with Devika's teacher about the dance, and help her go for a short part of practice so the fear shrinks instead of growing.

qa.q: What might Sonali be feeling as she sits on the bed?
qa.a: Sonali feels caring but uneasy, seeing the Monday pattern and worried it will get worse.

grounding: A girl's tummy ache keeps her home from dance practice, the fear vanishes at once, and she senses it will start earlier next time.

passage:
Last month I was supposed to read the news in the morning assembly. The night before, my stomach felt full of stones. I told Amma I felt sick, and she let me stay home.
The strange thing was how fast I felt fine. By ten o'clock I was eating biscuits and reading comics, happy as anything. It felt like I had escaped a trap.
Then Ma'am put my name down again for this Friday. This time my stomach started hurting on Tuesday. Tarun asked why I wasn't eating my lunch, and I said I had a bug. I don't. I think my tummy has learned that hurting gets me out of things.
I'm Harsha, and I'm scared the stones will come even earlier next time.

qa.q: What was Harsha supposed to do at the assembly?
qa.a: Read the news in the morning assembly.

qa.q: How did Harsha feel after staying home?
qa.a: Harsha felt a big rush of relief, as if a trap had been escaped.

qa.q: What could help Harsha before Friday?
qa.a: Telling Amma and Ma'am about the fear, and practising the news once in an empty classroom, so the relief of avoiding doesn't win again.

qa.q: What might Tarun think when told about a bug?
qa.a: Tarun might believe it and just feel sorry, not knowing the real fear behind it.

grounding: A child who stayed home from an assembly task felt instant relief, and now the stomach ache starts days earlier.

passage:
Note from Tanuja's mother, for the class teacher, Tuesday
On Sunday night Tanuja said her stomach hurt, and on Monday, the day of the maths oral test, she cried that she couldn't go. I let her stay home. An hour after the bus left, she was building a tent with her brother Dhruv and asking for pakoras.
Last night it started earlier. At dinner, before anyone mentioned school, she said, "What if my tummy hurts tomorrow?"
What I did next: this morning I told her I believed her tummy felt bad, that worry can do that, and that she would still go. I walked her to the gate. If the aches keep going or worry me, I'll check with our doctor. Could the oral test be tried again with you nearby?

qa.q: Who did Tanuja build a tent with on Monday?
qa.a: She built a tent with her brother Dhruv.

qa.q: Why did Tanuja's stomach ache disappear soon after the school bus left?
qa.a: The fear of the maths oral test dropped once school was avoided, and she felt relieved, so the ache faded.

qa.q: What turning point did Tanuja's mother choose, and why is it wise?
qa.a: She believed the tummy ache but still sent Tanuja to school with support, which stops avoidance from becoming the safe move while asking the teacher to help.

qa.q: How might Dhruv see Monday?
qa.a: Dhruv probably saw a fun day building a tent with his sister and may not understand why she was home, or wonder why he couldn't stay home too.

grounding: Shows a child's stomach ache keeping her home from a test, the quick relief that follows, and the fear starting earlier the next time.
